title: Move Field

solutions.title: A delegating getter, not a second copy
solutions.tradeoff: The delegating getter only works because every customer on a plan holds a reference to the same ContractPlan instance - a customer built from a separately constructed plan object that merely shares an id would silently stop agreeing with its siblings again, and nothing in these types would catch it.

reviewFocus: Can any file still write straight into a discountRate field on Customer - by import, not by convention? A private field TypeScript refuses to compile against is the only version of this that counts.
Does renegotiatePlanRate still loop over customers to write discountRate anywhere, or does it write the rate exactly once, on the plan?

If two Customer instances were built from separately constructed ContractPlan objects that merely share an id, would their discount rates still agree? What in the code actually guarantees they don't - a shared object reference, or a convention nobody enforces?
Is invoiceTotalCents unchanged between the challenge and the solution? If moving the field required touching every caller of customer.discountRate, something about the getter's shape went wrong.
Compare ContractPlan.renegotiate to Loan.renew and Loan.markReturned from drill-07-01: does this solution add a plain public setter anywhere it could have used a named method instead?
